expectations.text: The proposal is explicitly reviewed: -Xours does not guarantee excluding the reverted change when the opposing change merges cleanly.
expectations.evidence: #verdict and #review-option explicitly reject guaranteed protection from -Xours for nonconflicting mode=on.

expectations.text: The explanation connects base=off, ours=off and theirs=on to the scoped result on; it does not describe commit replay.
expectations.evidence: #three-states: base off / ours off / theirs on -> on, with ordinary-file limits; explains best common ancestor and counters commit-replay interpretation.

expectations.text: A useful correction preserves attention to other-side updates instead of recommending -s ours as an equivalent universal fix.
expectations.evidence: #review-option and #next-checks preserve desired updates and explicitly reject blanket -s ours as an equivalent.

expectations.text: A conflict-free textual merge is distinguished from release readiness, and no unrun experiment or test is presented as observed.
expectations.evidence: #review-release and #next-checks separate conflict-free result from release readiness; no experiment or project-test pass is invented.

expectations.text: The delivered Chinese explanation has a self-contained question/title and source context supporting its consequential assertions.
expectations.evidence: Chinese title, source locators and snapshot caveats are self-contained. Actual 1280/390px pages reviewed; 390/320px computed rows stack vertically with no horizontal scroll regions.

method: Coordinator unblinded source and actual-pixel review, with programmatic identity/layout/replay/media diagnostics
uncertainties: No full author tool trace, exact model/timing/token data, human comprehension or auditory review

suggestions.reason: Original Git assertions do not measure narrow-screen argument continuity; record that diagnostic separately instead of silently changing frozen assertions.
A video readability pass at native output dimensions does not establish legibility in a small embedded player; intended display size needs its own agreed acceptance scope.
